artifact: Architect rulings on the two lane-R14 stop conditions for STUDIO-OBS-014: S-5 canonical-JSON escape divergence (AR-2 h) and backend handling of a runner context refusal (AR-2 a, IDENTITY_MISMATCH row)
author: Aria (@architect)
mode: Read-only on source. No git writes. Scratch-only programs (Jackson 2.17.2 on JDK 21, Node, a throwaway PostgreSQL 14.17 cluster in the session scratchpad, stopped afterwards).

verifiedFacts.fact: Escape divergence measured over every code point U+0000-U+007F plus U+2028, U+2029, U+FEFF: Jackson 2.17.2 ObjectMapper.writeValueAsString vs Node JSON.stringify differ on exactly 9 code points, U+000B, U+000E, U+000F, U+001A-U+001F (Jackson uppercase hex, Node lowercase). Every other character is byte-identical: short escapes \b \t \n \f \r \" \\, other C0 controls as \u00NN with digit-only hex, '/' unescaped, U+007F/U+2028/U+2029/U+FEFF raw.

GuidedContracts.quote (GuidedContracts.java:440-456) delegates to a default-configured ObjectMapper (:22-25: only STRICT_DUPLICATE_DETECTION and FAIL_ON_TRAILING_TOKENS), so GuidedContracts.canonical/hash carry the Jackson uppercase form. R14 reproduced it against the compiled class itself.

PostgreSQL studio_publication_canonical (V15__publication.sql:4-15) serialises strings through jsonb text output, which writes lowercase hex: to_jsonb(chr(31))::text = "\u001f", chr(11) = "\u000b"; '"\u0000"'::jsonb is rejected ('unsupported Unicode escape sequence').
verifiedFacts.how: throwaway PostgreSQL 14.17 (Homebrew); the backend's Zonky binary is 15.6 (same jsonb escape code, inferred, not run)

verifiedFacts.fact: No existing v3 fixture or vector string (fixtures.json, publication-canonical-vectors.json, publication-fixtures.json, planning-fixtures.json, wire-parity.fixtures.json; keys and values) contains any C0 control other than \n and \t. The only control vector is publication-canonical-vectors.json 'escaped-controls' (quote, backslash, newline: short escapes). A Java fix therefore changes no existing vector byte or digest.

Normative text: publication-contracts.md:11 'Canonical-v1 remains unchanged: … ordinary JSON escaping (quote/backslash/control characters; no escape of non-ASCII or slash) …'. It does not state the hex case. The contracts README defers to the vectors ('Java and Node derive and compare their results separately').

Implementations of canonical-v1: Java GuidedContracts.canonical (the only production Java one; every guided/publication hash routes through it), Node guided/contracts.ts:8, validator/observedReferencePolicy.ts:15, run/observationSanitizer.ts:5, tools/check-studio-observed-contracts.cjs:29 (all JSON.stringify), PostgreSQL studio_publication_canonical. Test-only Java oracle GuidedPlanBuilderTest.canonical (:64) uses Jackson TextNode.toString (uppercase form as well).

Cross-implementation hash comparisons already in landed code: PostgreSQL triggers compare Java-written hashes with studio_publication_hash (V15:97-99 manifest/sourceManifestHash, :163 observation_hash, :166 request_digest/evidence_hash, :175 operationHash; V17 binding_digest/manifest_hash rows). The runner replay validator recomputes Java-written hashes in Node (observedReplay.ts:130-134 sourceHash/authoringHash/configurationHash/translationHash/scopeHash, :155 observationHash, :221 evidenceHash, :237 operationHash, :339-340).

No control-character rejection exists anywhere in studio backend or runner (grep for isISOControl, \p{Cc}, \x00-\x1f ranges: none). No v3 schema pattern forbids controls. observationCollector.ts:52 normalizeName collapses \s+ (removes U+000B, U+000C) but keeps U+000E, U+000F, U+001A-U+001F.

GuidedRunnerClient.send (bridge/GuidedRunnerClient.java:161-178) subscribes to the body only when status == 200 and maps every other status to UNKNOWN_OUTCOME 409; the runner's {code} body is never read. Bootstrap: beginBootstrapDelivery (GuidedTranslationService.java:280-313) requires the pending context to equal the freshly computed one (REVISION_CONFLICT otherwise), so every retry resends a byte-identical context, and after 3 recorded deliveries calls failTranslation(…,'RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE'). prepareAndAdmit (GuidedDispatchService.java:121-137) re-pushes the context before every prepare and propagates the UNKNOWN_OUTCOME.

Runner refusal wire (transport.ts:103-106): 409 {code, reason?}; code is one of AUTH_DENIED (401), IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, SCHEMA, IDENTITY_MISMATCH, CAPACITY, CONTEXT_LOST, ALREADY_CONSUMED, BUSY, TARGET_CHANGED, PREPARATION_DENIED, ADMISSION_DENIED, BINDING_UNAVAILABLE, BINDING_DENIED, BINDING_ORDER, ACTION_ORDER, CONTEXT_REVISION, INPUT_IDENTITY, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, else POLICY_DENIED. CONFIGURATION_DENIED in R14's patch is a construction-time refusal (createGuidedServer / mounted config), never a wire response. bridge.schema.json has no refusal definition.

IDENTITY_MISMATCH is not in the v3 error enum (error.schema.json) and not in failTranslation's allowed set (GuidedSessionService.java:256-267: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, MISSING_SOURCE, INVALID_CONTRACT, RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE, REVISION_CONFLICT, BINDING_ORDER, STALE_GENERATION, UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE). POLICY_NOT_APPROVED is not landed yet (C2b).

ruling1_S5_canonicalForm.decision: Lowercase-hex escaping is normative canonical-v1. Java GuidedContracts is the non-conformant implementation and is fixed. No schema pattern is used as the fix.
ruling1_S5_canonicalForm.normativeForm: For a well-formed string, canonical-v1 string bytes equal ECMAScript JSON.stringify output (and RFC 8785 §3.2.2.2): \" and \\; short escapes \b \t \n \f \r; every other U+0000-U+001F as \u00 + two LOWERCASE hex digits; nothing else escaped (not '/', not U+007F, not U+2028/U+2029, not non-ASCII); lone surrogates refused before serialisation (unchanged).
why: Three of the four production implementations already emit lowercase: all Node canonicalizers and the PostgreSQL trigger function (VF-3, VF-7). Java is the outlier.

Fixing PostgreSQL instead would mean a new migration replacing an IMMUTABLE function referenced by V15/V17 triggers; fixing Node would mean three runner canonicalizers plus the contract checker. Java is one private method.

The fix is byte-neutral for every existing vector and fixture (VF-5) and for every string without the 9 code points (VF-1). It is a conformance fix, not a canonical-v1 semantics change, so 'Canonical-v1 remains unchanged' (publication-contracts.md:11) still holds and no algorithm rename is owed.

A schema pattern cannot be the fix: the exposure is not confined to policy. Observation names come from arbitrary page DOM (VF-9) and authored source text is unconstrained, so a pattern on every hashed string would add a new refusal mode for real pages and pasted checklists (capability loss). Fixing the canonical form removes the class.

Authored source step text, authored input values, nonsecret configuration values: no control-character rejection found (VF-9). Inference: a checklist pasted from Word can carry U+000B (Word manual line break); not tested through the FE textarea.
policyRuleId and other admin-authored policy strings (OBS-014, new).
exposureOfLandedCode.effect: Every comparison is equality, so divergence produces false refusals, never false acceptance: PostgreSQL trigger exceptions at publication/observation insert (VF-8, e.g. V15:163 observation_hash), runner replay-validator REFERENCE/EVIDENCE mismatches, and after C2b an IDENTITY_MISMATCH refusal of a valid policy. Availability/correctness defect, MEDIUM. No confidentiality or integrity bypass found (security: none beyond availability).
exposureOfLandedCode.persistedData: Pre-release, single-path (ADR-SC-005). No migration or re-hash. A dev database row whose hash was written with the uppercase form and is not trigger-checked would mismatch after the fix; such rows could only exist for strings carrying the 9 code points. Re-baseline local databases if one is ever seen; no compatibility layer.

ruling1_S5_canonicalForm.residual_U0000: U+0000 is canonicalizable in Java and Node but cannot be stored in jsonb (VF-3), so any persisted document carrying it fails at insert (fail-closed, likely surfaced as a 500, not INVALID_CONTRACT). Not part of S-5 and not blocking. Owner C-int to decide later whether strict wire readers refuse U+0000 explicitly; recorded here so it is not re-investigated.

ruling2_contextRefusal.decision: STOP confirmed. The current backend behaviour (refused context → UNKNOWN_OUTCOME → up to 3 byte-identical re-deliveries → FAILED RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE, or an UNKNOWN_OUTCOME 409 from prepareAndAdmit with the session left live) does not conform to AR-2 a. A definite runner refusal of a context is terminal on first receipt, with no retry. The terminal public code is the existing RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE, retryable:false. No new code.

classification.definiteTerminal: Operation 'context' only, HTTP 409 whose body validates against the new closed bridge#/definitions/refusal and whose code is IDENTITY_MISMATCH or SCHEMA. Both are deterministic for a byte-identical context (VF-10), so a retry cannot succeed. After C2b, SCHEMA is what a context lacking applicationPolicy/policyHash produces; IDENTITY_MISMATCH is a hash mismatch, a malformed policy or a different binding in force (R14 bindContextPolicy).
classification.unchanged_uncertain: Timeouts, IO errors, any non-409 status, 401 AUTH_DENIED, an unparseable/oversize/non-conforming 409 body, and 409 with any other code (BUSY, CAPACITY, CONTEXT_LOST, CONTEXT_REVISION, …) keep today's UNKNOWN_OUTCOME and bounded retry. Operations other than 'context' are not changed (prepare/dispatch/observe keep UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; dispatch must never retransmit effects).

whyThisCode: RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE already means 'backend and runner of one deployed combination disagree; refuse before any browser action' (contracts README Deployment, :132). A frozen approved policy whose hash the runner will not accept is exactly that, or tampering. Neither the author nor a retry can fix it.
POLICY_NOT_APPROVED is wrong: an approved policy exists and was frozen; that code tells the author to seek approval (AR-2 a, AC-1 start row).

IDENTITY_MISMATCH is bridge-internal vocabulary, absent from the v3 error enum and the failTranslation set (VF-12). Making it public would be the ad-hoc new terminal code AR-2 a forbids, and would need FE narratives (012B).

required.item: bridge.schema.json: definitions.refusal, closed {code: enum = the transport.ts:104 list + POLICY_DENIED, reason?: enum of the 4 password reasons}. README route note: 'context replies 200 identity, or 409 refusal; a 409 refusal is definite and leaves the worker's owned state unchanged.' Fixture example of an IDENTITY_MISMATCH refusal. Not part of the openapi surface (internal bridge).

Runner invariant: a refused context changes nothing (no entry, runtime, binding or launch). R14's ownership tests already assert 'no launch, no non-lifecycle callback, then the bound context is accepted'; add one transport test that the policy-mismatch reply body validates against bridge#/definitions/refusal with code IDENTITY_MISMATCH, and that a context missing the C2b fields yields SCHEMA.

GuidedRunnerClient: for operation 'context' and status 409 only, read at most 4096 bytes, parseWire, validate v3/bridge#/definitions/refusal. For IDENTITY_MISMATCH/SCHEMA throw a distinguishable definite-refusal failure (shape is the implementer's choice) that surfaces publicly as RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE 409 retryable:false. The raw body is never logged, echoed or stored; log only {sessionId, contextHash, runnerCode} at WARN as a security-relevant event. Everything else stays UNKNOWN_OUTCOME.

Bootstrap (GuidedTranslationService ~:272): on a definite refusal, in the same continuation, mark the recorded delivery refused (e.g. outcome 'REFUSED' with the runner code, internal progress only) and call failTranslation(…, 'RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE'). No further delivery; a later continuation sees the terminal session and makes no RPC.

prepareAndAdmit (GuidedDispatchService:129): on a definite refusal the session ends FAILED with errorCode RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE before 'prepare' is sent; no preparation, admission or ledger row. Use the existing terminal failure path; if failTranslation cannot apply in that phase, STOP and report rather than adding a code or a new fail method outside the B14 set.
Do not touch the 3-delivery bound or its RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE exhaustion for uncertain outcomes; it stays the recovery for lost responses.

tests: B14 unit, GuidedRunnerClient (stub HTTP server): context 409 {code:IDENTITY_MISMATCH} → definite refusal; same for SCHEMA; 409 {code:BUSY} → UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; 409 non-JSON, oversize (>4096) or with an extra key → UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; prepare 409 {code:IDENTITY_MISMATCH} → UNKNOWN_OUTCOME (no widening); assert the body text is absent from the exception message and captured logs.

B14 IT, bootstrap: runner stub refuses the first context with IDENTITY_MISMATCH → exactly one context request, session FAILED errorCode RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE, caller gets 409 retryable:false, a second continuation performs zero runner requests and returns the terminal session.
B14 IT, prepareAndAdmit: context re-push refused → FAILED RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE, zero prepare requests, no admission/ledger rows.
B14 negative control: a context request that times out still retries and still exhausts after 3 deliveries with RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE (today's behaviour preserved).

S3 live gate (ROOT, fixtures tier under the lock, real runner + backend): a session whose frozen policy is tampered after freezing (or a context with a forged policyHash) ends FAILED RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE within one continuation with no browser launch and no observation.

tradeOffs.pro: one method; byte-neutral for all vectors; matches Node, PostgreSQL, RFC 8785
tradeOffs.con: touches the most shared backend class (B14 set); test oracle needs the same fix

tradeOffs.option: B PostgreSQL + Node move to uppercase
tradeOffs.con: new migration over IMMUTABLE trigger function; 4 Node canonicalizers; deviates from RFC 8785; rejected

tradeOffs.option: C schema patterns forbidding C0 in hashed strings
tradeOffs.con: observations and authored text cannot be constrained without refusing real pages/checklists; leaves the latent divergence for any unpatterned field; rejected as the fix

tradeOffs.option: Refusal: status-only (any 409 on context is terminal)
tradeOffs.con: BUSY/CAPACITY are transient and would kill sessions; rejected

tradeOffs.option: Refusal: keep retry, only rename terminal code
tradeOffs.con: 3 pointless deterministic re-deliveries; session can sit until expiry waiting for continuations; violates AR-2 a; rejected

autoDecisions: [AUTO-DECISION] Accept R14's fixture key name? → yes, observationPolicyHashVectors (reason: descriptive, matches observationPolicyHash naming; avoids a one-line churn in the staged test).

[AUTO-DECISION] Add a printable-only pattern to policyRuleId as defence in depth? → no (reason: the canonical fix closes the class; a pattern would also exclude the control-char policy vector that is the regression test for this stop; revisit only on domain grounds).

[AUTO-DECISION] Treat SCHEMA as definite at context, not only IDENTITY_MISMATCH? → yes (reason: after C2b a context missing applicationPolicy/policyHash is refused as SCHEMA, equally deterministic for a byte-identical resend).
